svg.title: Broker Point Ranges by Product
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-broker-point-ranges; chapter number: 2; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Broker Point Ranges by Product; subtitle: Stated ranges and worked examples from practitioners; unit: broker points (% of funded amount); caption: Points vary sharply by product, from a single point on USDA B&I loans to double-digit points on some equipment deals.; assumptions note: Typical values are the worked examples each speaker gave. The Equipment Finance Academy bar borrows Walton's $500k equipment example at 4% as its typical marker.; note: Sources are Shane Walton of the Commercial Loan Broker Institute, Eric Johnson of North Avenue Capital via Commercial Capital Training Group, Josh Feinberg of Leads For Locals, and Equipment Finance Academy.; bars: label: Most financing products (Walton); min: 1; max: 6; typical: 1.5; display: 1% to 6%, outliers to 15%; $2M at 1.5 points pays $30,000; label: Broker point range (Walton); min: 1; max: 10; typical: 1; display: 1 to 10 points; $2M at 1% pays $20,000; label: USDA B&I loans (Johnson); min: 1; max: 2; typical: 1; display: Lender charges 2, usually passes 1; 1 point on $4-5M = $70,000-$80,000; label: Equipment deals (Feinberg); min: 3; max: 15; typical: 7.5; display: 3 to 15 points, 7.5-8% average across 10 years; label: Equipment deals (Equipment Finance Academy); min: 1; max: 5; typical: 4; display: 1% to 5%, $2,000 to $5,000 per deal
